subject: Bridgehead slate — temporal carveout request for AlphaHealth benchmarking run
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Request: short-term dedicated window for AlphaHealth benchmark

Team —

AlphaHealth asked if we can carve out a short dedicated window for a full-stack benchmarking run next week. Summary:
- When: Nov 30 04:00 UTC -> Dec 1 08:00 UTC (~28 hours) but they may ask to extend to 36h for final validation.
- Why: they want stable latency/cost numbers for an internal procurement committee — cannot tolerate preemption noise.
- Need: ~8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (or 16 x V100-equivalent) fenced off from preemptible autoscale during the window.
- Asks: autoscale policy exemption (no preemption), tagging for cost attribution, and an ops contact.

They've shared a runbook draft and a capacity sheet (attached). Can we triage feasibility quickly? I flagged this as a temporary "bridgehead" carveout to avoid confusing it with pilot carveouts.

Quick answers needed by EOD tomorrow so we can confirm with them.

Thanks —
Aditya
Aditya Rao
Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:01:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Request: short-term dedicated window for AlphaHealth benchmark

Adding context from Product:
- This run is for a final benchmark before a procurement decision; AlphaHealth needs reproducible tail-latency numbers and token-cost curves.
- They will run a mix of chat + batch embedding workloads (2 models concurrently): ~1.5k concurrent chat sessions peak, and periodic batch embed jobs.

Can we get estimates for the GPU count vs expected 99th latency with/without preemption? If we can't guarantee no-preempt, we should offer a nominal SLA (e.g., 99th latency degradation <= 15%).

Also: they asked about the possibility to pin a model variant to a dedicated runtime to avoid kernel warmup variance. Is that something infra can support for a short window?

-Laura
Product Manager

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:46:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Request: short-term dedicated window for AlphaHealth benchmark

Kimberly/Dev — tagging for infra feasibility. Quick notes from capacity planning:
- 8 A100-eq reserved for 28-36h is plausible if scheduled during a low-utilization window (we're short on spare at month-end).
- Autoscale exemption (no preemption) requires ops to create a temporary "reservation" with manual override on eviction policy. That means we must disable preemptible spillover for those slots — doable but will impact burst capacity for other customers.
- Need a cost cap and sign-off (finance/CS) if AlphaHealth wants guaranteed non-preemptible SLA.

Dev — can you scope effort for (a) pinned runtime (kernel warmup suppression) and (b) a temporary reservation + runbook gating? If we can get runbook + instrumentation we could accept a 48h window as an exception with conditions.

Marcus
Capacity Planning

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:19:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Request: short-term dedicated window for AlphaHealth benchmark

Brief infra feasibility check:
- Pinned runtime: we can allocate a pinned runtime image per model for the window — this requires pre-provisioning the container images and ensuring KV cache warmup. I'll need the model names and expected sequence lengths to prepare cache priming. ~2 engineer-hours to prepare, ~1 hour to roll back.
- Reservation + eviction policy: we can create a temporal reservation with eviction disabled, but only if AlphaHealth signs a cost-overrun cap and accepts limited burst fallback. Implementation: create a reservation object in control plane, tag resources, and flip eviction flag for the window. Ops on-call must be looped.
- Instrumentation: must enable token-level latency tracing and cost tags. We'll require a filtered telemetry stream to AlphaHealth's contact and our CS.

Constraints: if we block those GPUs from the preemptible pool, it will reduce overall burst capacity for other small pilots that day. Recommend scheduling for Nov 30 00:00 UTC start (local low usage) and run for 36h to cover their validation.

I can support but need explicit approval from Kimberly + CS/Finance on cost guard rails.

-Dev

From: Jane Dawson <jane.dawson@alphahealth.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:34:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Bridgehead slate — temporal carveout request for AlphaHealth benchmarking run

Thanks for the quick triage — we can accept the conditions below but need the following commitments in writing before we confirm:
1) A 36-hour non-preemptible reservation for 8 A100-eq GPUs (Nov 30 00:00 UTC—Dec 1 12:00 UTC).
2) Instrumentation: token-level latency traces and a cost tag on every job.
3) A single ops contact for the window and a runbook for rollback in case of hardware issues.
4) A firm cost cap of $X (we will provide PO after you confirm the cap).

Attached is a slightly updated runbook with their internal test schedule. Please confirm by Friday EOD PST; otherwise we risk slipping their procurement committee timeline.

—Jane
AlphaHealth, Director of Cloud Engineering

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Jane Dawson <jane.dawson@alphahealth.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Bridgehead slate — temporal carveout request for AlphaHealth benchmarking run

Summary and decision:
Thanks everyone — after weighing product impact and procurement risk, I approve a one-time temporal carveout with the following binding conditions:
- Reservation: 36-hour non-preemptible reservation starting Nov 30 00:00 UTC for 8 A100-eq GPUs.
- Pinned runtime: Dev to provision pinned runtimes for the two model variants and prime KV caches before the window.
- Instrumentation: token-level tracing + cost tagging must be enabled and accessible to AlphaHealth CS during the run.
- Cost guard rails: CS/Finance to confirm final cost cap. AlphaHealth must sign a PO that includes the cap before we flip the reservation.
- Ops on-call + runbook: Dev to produce final runbook doc and ops contact. Ops will have rollback playbook and approval authority for early termination.

Action items:
- Dev: share pinned runtime image names and a short preflight checklist by Mon 29 Nov 12:00 UTC.
- Aditya: confirm PO timeline and provide the final AlphaHealth contact for billing.
- Marcus: create reservation object and reserve tagging; do not flip eviction flag until we have PO + runbook.
- Laura: agree on any SLA language we give AlphaHealth for the run's 99th latency.

I'll sign off on the reservation once the PO + runbook are in place.

Kimberly Park
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
